why: A branded primitive (number & { readonly [brand]: true }, string & { __kind: 'Slug' }) is a value of its primitive: the object member exists only for the checker (common.mjs primitiveBrand). As a Set item or a Map key it is compared by SameValueZero on that primitive, so the ordinary lane keys it by value (translate.mjs keyByValue; its carrier is an opaque type with equality, as a type parameter's is); the lint reads it as no object (lint.mjs isPrim) and === on a branded string, boolean or bigint as a value comparison; lane B draws it as its primitive (spec.mjs). Before, all three read it as an object: the Set and the Map were refused reference-key, === was refused reference-equality, and lane B drew a fake object. collapsedOf returns the membership through an if statement: proved, PASS-bounded. sameSlug negates a comparison of two branded strings: not proved, WITNESS (=== on a branded number stays refused reference-equality: its carrier is opaque with an equality and === is not reflexive on NaN). distinct drops the Set: a repeated id tells them apart, not proved, WITNESS. hits is untouched: proved, PASS-bounded. seenTwice tests the size in place of the membership: not proved, WITNESS.
